title: Fluid density transitions and grouped-row affordances for virtual table
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce fluid density transitions and improved grouped-row affordances for the virtualized table component. This ticket covers the visual language, interaction model, accessibility behavior, and performance constraints for smooth density animations, keyboard-first column resizing, and sticky grouped headers that survive aggressive row virtualization.
acceptance_criteria: Density toggle between Comfortable / Default / Compact animates without layout jank on large tables (>50k rows) in our benchmark harness
Grouped rows preserve sticky group headers while windowing/virtualization does not cause missing header flashes
Keyboard-first column resize exists: arrow nudges and double-tap to auto-fit content width
Reduced motion and low-power device fallbacks disable non-essential animations and maintain readability
Design tokens updated for compact density (spacing, font-size, token names documented) and added to token migration guide
design_notes: Key idea: treat density changes as a composited transform where possible (scale + translate) rather than reflowing size properties. We will animate padding and transform on a composition-only layer; cell content will use transform/opacity for cross-fade when necessary. For grouped rows, implement a lightweight sticky header layer above the virtualized list that queries the virtual window to render current group label and small summary chips. Column-resize will use a drag handle with easing and snap heuristics (content-based snap points + user override). Accessibility: live-region announcements for column width changes and group header transitions; focus retention during density switch; ensure all interactions are reachable via keyboard and screen readers. Performance budget: 16ms jank budget per frame at 60fps for user interactions; run perf tests in the runtime-1.18 benchmark harness.
tradeoffs: Animating padding and font-size may be visually expensive; chosen approach uses transform/scale with clipped content to avoid full reflow at the expense of more complex clipping logic
Sticky header overlay duplicates minimal DOM for group headers rather than attempting to render all headers inside virtualized DOM, trading slight implementation complexity for visible stability
Auto-fit heuristics prefer sampling cell content widths rather than measuring entire dataset to reduce overhead, which may mis-predict for highly variable content
Enabling certain animations by default improves discoverability but hurts low-power devices; we opt for opt-out via prefers-reduced-motion and a Console toggle
decisions: Use a separate sticky header overlay for grouped rows instead of relying on in-window top-most rendered row
Implement density transitions with CSS transforms and opacity cross-fades where possible
Expose keyboard resize interactions: left/right arrows nudge by 4px, shift+arrows nudge by 16px, double-press Enter triggers auto-fit
Fallback: on devices reporting low-power mode or when frame time exceeds threshold, switch to instant density changes (no animation)
